validity.researcher_notes: Same underlying evidence as the P5114 concern, restated for Phase 2. DT Midstream's Aug 2023 investor presentation (https://s28.q4cdn.com/581450200/files/doc_presentations/2023/Aug/22/dtm-company-presentation-august-2023-vf.pdf, verified: contains 'LEAP') lists Phase 2 expansion (Q1 2024, +0.4 Bcf/d) alongside the same slide's statement that 'Project includes a combination of looping and compression,' and names 'LEAP pipeline looping' as a key project update positioned against the Phase 2 line in the growth-investment table. DT Midstream's FY2023 10-K (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1842022/000184202224000003/dtm-20231231.htm, verified: contains '209-mile') confirms LEAP had grown to a '209-mile lateral pipeline' by Dec 31, 2023, immediately after Phase 1 was placed in service and while Phase 2 construction was underway — up from the ~150-155 miles reported before the phase program began, consistent with new pipe (not compression alone) being added. Oil & Gas Journal (https://www.ogj.com/pipelines-transportation/pipelines/article/55240028/dt-midstream-expanding-haynesville-marcellus-natural-gas-pipeline-systems, verified: contains 'looping') independently describes the same phased LEAP program as using 'incremental compression and looping.' This row's Capacity=400.00 MMcf/d matches the Phase 2 capacity figure (400 MMcf/d, 1.3->1.7 Bcf/d) reported in DT Midstream's Dec 2023 mechanical-completion announcement and Gas Compression Magazine's coverage of it, confirming the row-to-phase match is correct. I found no Phase-2-specific mileage or diameter breakdown isolating what portion (if any) of the 54-mile system growth belongs to Phase 2 versus Phase 1, so I am not filling Diameter directly rather than risk a fabricated per-phase figure (standing rule 2). Marking this a concern, not UNRESOLVED, because the evidence actively contradicts a 'compression-only, blank is correct' resolution.
